How Photography Affects Size Perception
Macro (extreme close-up) photography is heavily utilized in jewelry listings, enabling viewers to examine pieces in larger-than-life detail. An accurate understanding of the actual sizes of these pieces cannot be deduced using photos alone. It is important that the bidder takes close note of the measurements and weights to determine actual sizes.
About Gemstone & Metal Testing
Gemstones are tested with a Presidium Gem Tester. Goodwill of the Olympics & Rainier Region is a member of the International Gem Society; however, as we are not certified gemologists, we cannot guarantee the authenticity of any gemstone unless otherwise stated. Gemstone identification information is provided for your reference and consideration in bidding; no guarantee is implied.
Pearls are tested with a check for grittiness to detect nacre irregularities. We are generally unable to specify pearl types and characteristics; they may be cultured, wild, freshwater or saltwater pearls. Coral may be natural or dyed; most of our coral listings include dyed pieces.
Metals including Gold, Silver, and Platinum are tested using an XRF precious metal analyzer, the Niton XL2 by Thermo Scientific, unless explicitly noted otherwise. XRF (X-ray fluorescence) analysis is a non-destructive testing method able to determine an item's elemental composition. Identification of other non-magnetic metals, including brass, bronze, copper, tin, and titanium, rely on our best estimation, and no guarantee is implied; they have not been tested or positively identified unless explicitly noted otherwise. Some jewelry may contain non-precious metals in clasps or findings, causing parts of the piece to respond to a magnet.

Rocket Nut Cracker - Metal and Wood Construction
Vintage, Arthur W. Reed Manufacturing Co.
The Reed's Rocket Nut Cracker is a classic piece of American mid-century kitchen engineering, manufactured by the Arthur W. Reed Manufacturing Co. in Little Rock, Arkansas. Designed to provide "commercial speed to a formerly tedious job," this manual cracker uses a powerful lever-action mechanism to split shells while keeping the nut meats intact. The original cardboard box is included and shows significant wear, including tears, creases, and age-related discoloration. A vintage "Dixie Mart" price sticker is present on the box top.

description:
Thomas America Series Model BD 117A
Norman Rockwell Collector's Edition Radio and Cassette Player
AM/FM/AFC Bands
The Thomas America Series Model BD 117A is a cathedral-style tabletop radio that pays homage to the golden age of broadcasting. This collector's edition features branding inspired by the iconic American illustrator Norman Rockwell, housed in a classic wood cabinet that captures the aesthetic of the 1930s. Produced as part of a nostalgic reproduction series, this unit combines traditional styling with a built-in cassette player, making it a functional decor piece for vintage audio enthusiasts.
Hand-crafted wood cabinet with arched cathedral top and decorative speaker grille work
Full AM/FM/AFC radio functionality with analog tuning, volume, and tone control knobs
Discreet side-loading cassette tape deck with auto-stop feature
Original Thomas America Series and Norman Rockwell brass-tone identification plates
Condition:
The wood cabinet is in good cosmetic condition with light surface wear and minor scuffs consistent with age, primarily on the base and side edges. All four front control knobs (Volume, Tone, Tuning, Band Selector) are present and functional. The side-loading cassette door and mechanism appear intact. The back panel is secure and all original identification stickers are legible. The unit has been tested and powers on.
